Yes. I would treat these exactly as we treated traditions: **candidate corpora to enumerate first, before interpreting them**. For each \(N\), we want every materially different native use of that count, its factorization, its object type, and whether \(N\) is a base population, address space, generated realization, process length, container, or mathematical consequence.

The first-pass map I would use is below. I am deliberately including **weak/null-control fields** as well as rich ones; otherwise we'll bias ourselves toward numbers that conveniently “work.”

| \(N\) | Highest-value candidate corpus fields | Native / candidate generative shapes to investigate | Why it matters / what to test | Priority |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **64** | **Yijing hexagrams**; Indian **64 Yoginīs**; 64 kalās/arts; Tantric 64-fold corpora; Vāstu 8×8 grids; chess as historical combinatorial control; **64 genetic codons** as modern biological control; binary/computation | \(8\times8\); \(2^6\); six binary decisions; \(4^3\) | We already know Yijing gives a genuine \(8\times8=64\) compositional state space. Now test whether Indian 64s are also generated lattices or merely enumerated classes. Genetics gives an extraordinary independent control: \(4^3=64\) symbols from three positions over a four-letter alphabet. **Same cardinality, completely different generator.** | **VERY HIGH** |
| **72** | Shem triplets; 72 angel names; Goetia/Rudd; Greco-Egyptian **72 pentads**; decans×2; 72 translators of the Septuagint tradition; Luke's **70/72 disciples textual variant**; 72 languages/tongues traditions; Confucian 72 disciples/sages; Solomonic/Islamicate layers; astronomical 5° divisions | \(36\times2\); \(12\times6\); \(24\times3\); \(3\times24\); \(360/5\); F/R/F 72-column extraction | This is already our central bus. The next step is to separate **72[addresses], 72 triplets, 72 names, 72 actors, 72 paired roles** and reconstruct which later systems attach themselves to which earlier 72. The ancient 72-pentad lattice is already established. citeturn586920search0 | **CRITICAL** |
| **108** | **27 nakshatras ×4 padas**; Vedic/Jyotiṣa lunar addressing; Hindu/Jain/Buddhist mālā and recitation counts; Buddhist 108 afflictions/mental states; Japanese 108 temple-bell strikes; 108 names; Tibetan ritual enumerations; architecture/temple counts; sound/mantra preservation | \(27\times4\); \(\mathrm{LCM}(12,27)=108\); \(6\times3\times2\times3=108\) in one Buddhist explanatory scheme; \(12\times9\) | Very important because we already derived 108 **mathematically before treating it as sacred**: it is the minimum common resolution of 12 and 27. Then independently, nakshatras genuinely divide into four padas, producing 108. citeturn586920search143turn586920search144 | **CRITICAL** |
| **144** | Babylonian **12×12 microzodiac**; Indian varga astrology / **Dvādaśāṃśa** candidate; Revelation \(144{,}000\) and 144-cubit wall; nested 12-fold systems; music/computation controls | \(12\times12\); \(72\times2\); \(36\times4\); \(16\times9\) | We already found the Babylonian outer-12 × inner-12 architecture. This is ideal for testing **nested address spaces** versus “144 beings.” Revelation gives a completely different type: \(12\times12\times1000\), useful for scale amplification and symbolic multiplication. | **VERY HIGH** |
| **180** | Greek/Hellenistic astronomy and astrology; opposition aspect; semicircle/hemisphere; Vedic **half-year / ayana** structures; 360-day-year decompositions; six signs; lunar-calendar half cycles; geometry | \(360/2\); \(6\times30\); \(36\times5\); \(12\times15\); \(180+180=360\) | This should be studied mainly as a **polarity/half-cycle operator**, not as a population. Particularly useful for testing whether opposition is represented by complement \(i\mapsto i+N/2\). Vedic chronology also supplies explicit 180-day half-year schemes in some reconstructions. citeturn526641search62 | **HIGH** |
| **216** | **Shem source letters**: \(72\times3\); Plato/Pythagorean number tradition; music/harmonic arithmetic; cube symbolism; Buddhist/Hindu double-108 practices as secondary layer; 6³ spatial/cubic controls | \(\boxed{72\times3}\); \(6^3\); \(108\times2\); \(3^3+4^3+5^3=216\) | Extremely valuable because 216 emerges from two **independent structural routes already in our corpus**: three 72-letter Exodus verses / 72 triplets of three letters, and Greek mathematical speculation around the cube of six. The “Platonic number =216” identification is traditional but disputed, so it is a perfect provenance-sensitive test. citeturn526641search59turn526641search5 | **VERY HIGH** |
| **288** | **1 Chronicles Temple musicians**; Lurianic **288 sparks**; music/liturgy; Kabbalistic Four Worlds / divine-name calculations; 24 divisions; 72×4; possible restoration/tikkun architecture | \(\boxed{24\times12=288}\); \(\boxed{72\times4=288}\); \(32\times9\) as mathematical control | This one just became **extremely high-value**. 1 Chronicles explicitly gives **288 trained musicians organized as 24 groups of 12**. citeturn586920search1turn586920search6 Lurianic Kabbalah independently makes **288 sparks** a central restoration object; scholarship explicitly connects the number with fourfold 72-name calculations. citeturn358516search3 So we have **music + Kabbalah + 72 + restoration** meeting on a number we had not engineered toward. | **CRITICAL** |
| **300** | Hebrew Bible: **Gideon's 300**, Noah's ark **300 cubits**, Samson's 300 foxes/jackals; Greek **300 Spartans** as historical/literary control; architecture/metrology; possible sexagesimal \(5\times60\); ritual enumerations elsewhere | \(5\times60\); \(10\times30\); \(12\times25\) | Currently a **weak/heterogeneous number**, which is useful. We should test whether there is any genuine generative architecture tying its occurrences together or whether 300 is simply a convenient round magnitude. Biblical occurrences are real but functionally unrelated on first inspection. citeturn582662search2 | **MEDIUM / NULL CONTROL** |
| **324** | Indian 27/12 systems; lunar-zodiac cross-products; \(108\times3\) ritual possibilities; 36-fold systems ×9; \(18^2\); astronomical/state-product searches; magical-table corpora | \(27\times12=324\); \(108\times3\); \(36\times9\); \(18^2\) | **Especially valuable as an unresolved prediction.** I do **not** currently know a strong native ancient 324 architecture. That is good. The most interesting hypothesis is whether a tradition explicitly uses the **Cartesian product** \(27_{\rm nakshatra}\times12_{\rm zodiac}\), because the actual common spatial refinement is only 108. If 324 occurs, it would distinguish **pair-state space** from physical subdivision. Do not promote modern 324-recitation claims without old sources. | **HIGH AS FALSIFIER**, low historical support currently |
| **360** | Babylonian sexagesimal astronomy; Hellenistic zodiac; Egyptian 360+5 civil calendar; Vedic 360-day/year/wheel imagery; Greek geometry; decans; pentads; astrology; degrees; circular music/phase models; perhaps Mesopotamian divine-number systems | \(\boxed{12\times30}\); \(\boxed{36\times10}\); \(\boxed{72\times5}\); \(6\times60\); \(180\times2\); \(360+5\) calendar | This is probably the **principal carrier-scale corpus**. We already have three native resolutions of the same circle: 12 signs, 36 decans, 72 pentads. The question is no longer “why 360?” but **which
